sources: Bhagavata Purana, book 7 (Prahlada’s devotion to Vishnu; his father Hiranyakashipu tries many ways to stop him and fails)
Holika, Hiranyakashipu’s sister, and the bonfire: a festival story found in later tellings and widespread tradition
Holika Dahan, the bonfire on the night before Holi (the full moon of Phalguna)

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? are you still carrying an old grudge? it’s heavy. you’ve held it a while.
options: then let’s see what to do with it. listen.
then this one is for you. listen.

steps.line: Prince Prahlada was devoted to Vishnu. His father, a proud demon king, hated it.

steps.q: The king tries everything to stop his son from praying. What do you guess Prahlada does?
o: Prays in secret, to keep the peace
Leaves the palace to pray elsewhere
steps.why: Openly, every time. In the Bhagavata Purana the king tries weapons, snakes, elephants, poison and a cliff, and Prahlada keeps praying.

steps.line: He tried everything to stop him. Prahlada kept praying.
Then the king’s sister, Holika, tried a trick with a great bonfire, sure that fire could never touch her.

steps.q: Holika is sure fire can never touch her. What do you think happens?
o: Both walk out of the fire unharmed
steps.why: The fire takes Holika and spares Prahlada; many tellings say her fireproof shawl flew from her onto him. That’s why the bonfire is called Holika Dahan, the burning of Holika.

steps.line: But the fire turned on her, and Prahlada walked out untouched.

steps.q: The fire isn’t the end of the story. Who finally stops the cruel king?
o: Vishnu, as half man, half lion
steps.why: The king’s boon said no man or beast could kill him, by day or night, inside or out. So Vishnu came as Narasimha, half man, half lion, at dusk, on a doorstep.

steps.line: On the night before Holi, Hindus light bonfires to remember it, and many throw their old grudges into the fire.
steps.label: Holika Dahan

steps.q: Holi’s colors come with a second story. Whose?
steps.why: Young Krishna, it’s said, worried fair Radha wouldn’t love him with his dark skin. His mother said: color her face. Holi plays it out. (Rama’s homecoming is Diwali.)

steps.line: Let the old burn, so the new can start. The fire comes first. Then the colors.
steps.label: today

steps.q: You’re at a Holika bonfire with fresh-cut wheat in your hand. What do many families do with it?
o: Roast the grain in the flames
steps.why: Holi falls at the spring harvest. Many families roast green grain or coconut in the fire, walk around it, and share what they’ve roasted.

say: here’s what i love. the king had power, and holika had a trick. prahlada just had devotion, and it was enough.
hindus light holika’s bonfire to remember that goodness outlasts cruelty. and many say it’s the night to throw old grudges in, so the colors can start fresh.

steps.q: On Holi, colors are thrown at everyone: the boss, a stranger, a grandparent. What does that say about the day?
o: It’s a contest to color the most people
It’s only for family and close friends
Old ranks and grudges are set aside
steps.why: People shout “bura na mano, Holi hai”: don’t be offended, it’s Holi! Rank and old quarrels give way, for a day at least.

today.say: write one grudge on a piece of paper. then throw it away, or burn it safely. many families walk around the holika fire with a prayer. you can join a bonfire, learn the story with someone, or just let the paper go. it’s your choice.
options: then let it burn. tomorrow, colors.
I’m not ready to let it go
that’s honest. even writing it down loosens it.
